title: Bulgarian solitaire: the total settling time S(n) (a new exact sequence), with the worst-case settling time and its relation to A188160 (reproducible)
description: Exact functional-graph statistics of Bulgarian solitaire. An arrangement of n cards is a partition of n; one MOVE removes a card from every pile (empty piles vanish) and forms one new pile equal to the number of piles. The map is deterministic, so every arrangement runs down a transient 'tail' into a cycle. PRIMARY RESULT: a(n) = S(n) = the TOTAL settling time = the sum over all p(n) arrangements of the number of moves each needs to first become periodic (reach its cycle); computed exactly for n=1..55 (0, 0, 3, 3, 8, 33, 26, 41, 86, 267, 206, 242, 374, 831, 2133, ...), reported absent from OEIS by the computing session on 2026-06-26 (multiple windows + name search); this absence search is not logged in the artifact and is re-run by the human depositor at actual deposit time, with the query log committed then. It equals p(n) times the mean settling time of a random arrangement. SECONDARY (worst case): maxTail(n) = the largest settling time over all arrangements of n (0,0,2,2,3,6,4,5,7,12,...); also absent, but NOT independent — verified executably for n<=61 (in verify.mjs, against the OEIS A188160 b-file to n=61) that maxTail(n) = A188160(n) - A183110(n) + 1, where A188160 is the catalogued 'max steps until a partition repeats' (which bundles one full cycle) and A183110 is the longest cycle length; this is offered as a derived quantity and a verified-but-unproven structural relation (the worst-case transient always flows into a LONGEST cycle), NOT as a new independent sequence. CALIBRATION (the honesty anchor): the same engine reproduces, exactly, five catalogued sequences of this process -- the recurrent-state count = Pascal's triangle (Etienne 1991; A135278/A007318), the number of cycles A037306, the Garden-of-Eden count A123975, the longest cycle length A183110, and the unique-fixed-point-at-triangular-n theorem (Brandt 1982) -- AND the proven Igusa(1985)/Etienne(1991) tight bound maxTail(T_k) = k^2 - k at every triangular n; so only S(n) (and the auxiliary maxTail/maxTailCount) is claimed uncatalogued. S(n) is computed to n=55 two ways on one functional graph (reverse-BFS distance-to-cycle vs forward memoised iteration): these share partition enumeration, move, and cycle detection and differ only in the distance computation, and verify.mjs holds every term to this deposit's b-file; the independent guard against a shared graph bug is s_explore.py, a separate-language engine (own partitioner, move, cycle detection, forward-memo tails) that reproduces all 55 S(n) terms. PROVENANCE: computation and prose produced by an AI instance (Claude) in the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule; deposited as a citable, independently-checkable artifact and explicitly offered for independent human verification. Per OEIS policy it has NOT been submitted to OEIS by the project; any OEIS entry should be authored only by a human who has verified it themselves.
